title: The interruption reserve
hook: A toy team spends reserve capacity on interruptions. How much remains after four rounds?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Compute reserve depletion from sustained imbalance and identify when the zero floor is reached.

misconception: A small reserve is safe whenever the average team schedule appears full.
objective: Compute reserve depletion from sustained imbalance and identify when the zero floor is reached.

claims.text: Original stipulated feedback model: A inputs [4, 2, 3, 4] yield 0; B inputs [8, 2, 3, 4] yield 4. Prediction correct option 4. A ends with {A} reserve hours; B with {B}. Interruptions consume one more hour than is replenished each round, exhausting the smaller reserve. Reserve replenishment and interruption demand are invented; this is not a staffing or burnout model.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy reserve starts at 7 hours, replenishes 1 and spends 3 each round for two rounds. Reserve left? The reserve loses two hours each round: 7 − 2 − 2 = 3.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, feedback, inputs [7, 1, 3, 2], output 3; independent Python recomputation.
